newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia names Jakarta envoy, aims to boost ties.
newsitem.headline: Australia names Jakarta envoy, aims to boost ties.

text.p: Australia, moving to cement closer ties with neighbouring Indonesia, appointed a senior career diplomat as its new ambassador to Jakarta on Thursday in a bid to end a long-running wrangle over diplomatic postings.

Foreign Minister Alexander Downer, reaffirming the new conservative government's commitment to closer ties with Indonesia, said John McCarthy, currently ambassador to the United States, would soon replace Allan Taylor in Jakarta.
Relations between the two countries have moved to a firmer footing, Downer said in a statement from New York, where he is on an official visit.
"The government is committed to building on this solid foundation, consolidating recent gains and further deepening and broadening the relationship," Downer said.
A Canberra-based Asian diplomat said McCarthy's selection would end a long-running saga that has seen ambassadorial candidates rejected by each country amid protests and street demonstrations.
"Now this whole affair can be put behind them," he told Reuters.
"Both countries now have very capable, non-controversial ambassadors and they can concentrate on the relationship itself."

Relations between Jakarta and Canberra were hit by separate rows over diplomatic appointments earlier this year and in 1995, with violent public protests and flag-burnings in Australia and objections at senior levels in Jakarta.

A strong public outcry in mid-1995 forced Australia's former Labor government to reverse its initial acceptance of Indonesia's appointment of Lieutenant-General Herman Mantiri as ambassador to Canberra.
Mantiri's selection sparked protests and flag-burnings around the country over his description of the 1991 massacre of civilians in East Timor by Indonesian troops as "quite proper".
After leaving the post vacant for several months, Indonesia appointed respected career diplomat Wiryono Sastrohandoyo.

A year after the Mantiri row, Australia's new conservative Liberal-National government was forced to back down on its plan to send senior diplomat Miles Kupa, a former adviser to former foreign minister Garteh Evans, to Indonesia as ambassador.
Departmental briefings by Kupa critical of President Suharto's rule and the Suharto's family business interests, after an earlier stint in Jakarta, sparked strong criticism in Indonesia.
As Indonesian protests mounted, Kupa, seeking to head off a diplomatic row, asked Downer to withdraw his nomination.
McCarthy, 53, a former deputy secretary of the Foreign Affairs and Trade Department, has previously served as ambassador in Thailand, Laos, Mexico and Syria.
Analysts in Canberra said McCarthy's appointment also cleared the way for the long-anticipated selection of former conservative foreign minister Andrew Peacock as ambassador to the United States.
The Liberal-National coalition government, which ended 13 years of Labor Party rule in a landslide March election win, has begun appointing former coalition politicians to diplomatic postings.
Downer appointed former Liberal senator Michael Baume as consul-general to New York.
